# deltabox toolchain

> All-in-one development toolchain that let's you scaffold projects, generate and manage configs, tsconfigs, custom templates, syncing, changelogs, CI, Vite+, migrations, and more.

> If `https://toolchain.deltabox.studio` is unavailable, the same documentation is available in the repository at <https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/tree/main/apps/docs> (source Markdown).

This file is a concise, link-first overview. For the **full** documentation in a single file, see [`llms-full.txt`](https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/llms-full.txt).

**How it works** — `@deltabox/toolchain` is a config-driven toolchain:

- **One config.** `dbx.config.ts` exports `{ toolchain: { ...sections } }`; every section is opt-in by presence (`section: true` uses defaults, omit it to leave that area untouched).
- **Sync.** `dbx sync` runs each enabled section and writes the managed files, tracked in `.dbx/toolchain/manifest.json`; `dbx sync --check` is the CI gate. `dbx sync --recursive` syncs every discovered project in dependency order.
- **Nested configs.** A non-root `dbx.config.*` merges over the nearest ancestor config: objects merge, while scalars and arrays replace; `project.type` and `hooks` are never inherited.
- **Project graph.** `dbx projects` writes `.dbx/toolchain/projects.json` (workspace dirs + dependencies), used by `sync --recursive`, the VS Code view and per-workspace changelogs.
- **Sections.** `project`, `changelog`, `biome`, `tsconfig`, `templates`, `vite`, `watch`, `logger`, `providers`.
- **Runtime.** Node ≥ 22.5 and Yarn 4 (corepack); Vite+ (`vp`) resolves at the repo root.
